REGENT OF SINTANG
WEST KALIMANTAN PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF SINTANG,

Considering:

a. that all forms of acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination; b. that in addition to protection efforts, prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence are needed, so as to achieve the fulfillment, advancement, enforcement and protection of human rights universally and fundamentally; c. that in connection with the intention in letter b and in an effort to provide a legal basis for its implementation in Sintang Regency, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Sintang Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence; In View of:

1. Law Number 27 of 1959 concerning Stipulation of Emergency Law Number 3 of 1953 Concerning Establishment of Level II Regions in Kalimantan (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1953 Number 9, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 352) as Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1959 Number 72, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 1820); 2. Government Regulation Number 79 of 2005 concerning Guidelines for Development And Supervision of Regional Government Administration (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2005 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4593); 18.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person who is female by sex.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has a specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor about matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Doctor specializing in Psychiatry about the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 16
(1) Guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children shall be carried out by relevant Agencies in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of providing guidelines that include technical implementation of protection for women and children.
(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children shall be carried out by relevant Agencies together with government internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 7
Sufficiently clear

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children, thereby causing the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or child victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

CHAPTER XI
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 19
Every criminal act relating to the protection of women and children shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part
Institutional

1.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the only trafficking-related content is in the legal basis list (“Undang-Undang Nomor 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang”). The operative provisions defining “kekerasan” and the scope of violence (Pasal 1 angka 6–11; Pasal 3 ayat (2)) do not mention trafficking/perdagangan orang, and the regulation’s forms of violence are limited to physical, sexual, and psychological violence. Merely citing a national anti-trafficking law in the ‘Mengingat’ section does not mean the local regulation substantively includes human trafficking as an addressed form of violence. The judge over-inferred inclusion from a citation, so the false positive is best explained by evaluation failure (overly lenient reasoning).

1.9.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences define sexual violence and include forced intercourse for commercial purposes, but they do not explicitly address sexual exploitation or sexual slavery as distinct concepts.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, first and foremost is to protect all the people and the entire homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because such acts constitute crimes against human existence.

Article 3
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.
Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.
Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

1.9.rationale: The original Indonesian definition of sexual violence explicitly includes “pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial dan/atau tujuan tertentu” (Pasal 1 angka 11). Forced sex ‘for commercial purposes’ is a direct description of sexual exploitation (and is commonly treated as such in policy indicators). This exact content was present in the retrieved English candidates (the same definition). Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ was too strict, and the golden label ‘Yes’ appears consistent with the Indonesian text. The discrepancy is best attributed to evaluation failure (judge misapplied/over-narrowed the indicator), not retrieval/translation.

11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the matter and according to the manner regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.

22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

28. Police is all matters related to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY
NUMBER 8 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, first and foremost is to protect all the people and the entire homeland of Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because such acts constitute crimes against human existence.

Article 3
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.
Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.
Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

CHAPTER XII
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
Article 21
Further provisions regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 20
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children, thereby causing the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(2) Every person who commits acts of obstructing officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in carrying out protection and service efforts for women and/or child victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
(3) The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

5.6.rationale: The original Indonesian text mentions mass media only in the context of confidentiality/privacy protections (Pasal 5 huruf k: protection from publication of identity through mass media; Pasal 14 ayat (3) huruf g: maintain privacy/confidentiality including media reporting). This is not ‘media engagement’ as a stakeholder-engagement strategy (e.g., partnering with media, outreach campaigns, coordination mechanisms). The judge treated any mention of media as engagement, which is an overbroad interpretation. The golden label ‘No’ aligns with the Indonesian text, so this is an evaluation failure rather than a translation or retrieval problem.
